topics.name: Motion in a plane and uniform circular motion

questions.q: To describe the position of an object, we need a reference point and…
questions.a: the distance and direction of the object from the reference point
w: only the distance from the reference point
only the time at that instant
questions.e: Position = distance and direction from a fixed reference point at an instant of time.

questions.q: An object is said to be in motion when…
questions.a: its position with respect to a reference point changes with time
w: it is far away from the reference point
its position with respect to a reference point stays the same
questions.e: If the position changes with time, the object is in motion; if it does not change, the object is at rest.

questions.q: On a straight line, positions to the left of the origin O are generally taken as…
w: equal to the distance from O
questions.e: Positions to the right of O are taken as positive (+) and to the left as negative (–).

questions.q: Which of these is an example of motion in a straight line?
w: The tip of a clock's minute hand
A satellite going around the Earth
questions.e: A vertically falling ball moves along a straight line – linear motion.

questions.q: What is the difference between an instant of time and a time interval?
questions.a: An instant is a single clock reading; a time interval is the duration between two clock readings
w: A time interval is a single clock reading; an instant is the duration between two readings
They mean exactly the same thing
An instant is always exactly one second long
questions.e: An instant is one reading of the clock, a time interval is the duration between two instants.

questions.q: A bag lies on the seat of a moving train. For a passenger sitting in the train, the bag is…
questions.a: at rest, because its position relative to the passenger does not change
w: in motion, because the train is moving
questions.e: Rest and motion depend on the reference point. Relative to the passenger, the bag's position does not change.

questions.q: “The Earth moves around the Sun.” Can a book kept on a table on the Earth be called at rest?
questions.a: Yes, with respect to the Earth; but it is in motion with respect to the Sun
w: No, nothing on the Earth can ever be at rest
Yes, it is at rest with respect to every reference point
No, because the book has mass
questions.e: Whether an object is at rest or in motion depends on the chosen reference point.

questions.q: A girl's position on a straight track is –30 m. This means she is…
questions.a: 30 m from the origin, on the negative side
w: 30 m from the origin, on the positive side
questions.e: The number gives the distance from the origin and the sign gives the direction.

questions.q: Displacement is…
questions.a: the net change in position of an object between two instants of time
w: the total length of the path travelled
the distance of the object from the Earth
questions.e: Displacement = net change in position, with both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of distance travelled and displacement?
questions.e: Both distance travelled and displacement are measured in metres.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards and caught back at the same point. Its displacement is…
questions.e: It comes back to its starting position, so the net change in position is zero.

questions.q: Which statement about displacement is ALWAYS true?
questions.a: Its magnitude is less than or equal to the total distance travelled
w: Its magnitude can be greater than the total distance travelled
Its magnitude is less than the distance travelled in all cases
questions.e: Displacement can be zero, or equal to the distance (one direction), but never more than the distance.

questions.q: Total distance travelled and magnitude of displacement are equal when the object…
questions.a: moves in a straight line in one direction without turning back
w: moves with changing speed and turns back
questions.e: If the object never turns back, the path length equals the straight-line change in position.

questions.q: The fuel used up by a vehicle depends on…
questions.e: The engine works for the whole path covered, so fuel depends on distance, not displacement.

questions.q: An athlete runs from O to A (100 m) on a straight track and then runs back to B, which is 40 m from O. Her total distance and displacement are…
questions.e: Distance = OA + AB = 100 m + 60 m = 160 m; displacement = OB = 40 m in the positive direction.

questions.q: A student runs from the ground floor to the 4th floor, then comes down to the 2nd floor. Each floor is 3 m high. Total vertical distance and displacement?
questions.e: Up 4 floors = 12 m, down 2 floors = 6 m, so distance = 18 m. Final position is 2 floors = 6 m above the start.

questions.q: Father walks to a shop {d} m away on a straight road, comes back home for a bag, walks to the shop again and then returns home. What is the total distance he travelled?
questions.e: He covers the home–shop distance 4 times: 4 × {d} m = {ans} m. His displacement is 0 m because he ends at home.

questions.q: Father walks to a shop {d} m away on a straight road, comes back home for a bag, walks to the shop again and then returns home. What is his displacement from home?
questions.e: He ends where he started, so the net change in position is 0 m (even though he walked 4 × {d} m).

questions.q: Average speed is equal to…
questions.e: Average speed = total distance travelled / time interval (Eq. 4.1).

questions.q: Average velocity is equal to…
questions.e: Average velocity = change in position (displacement) / time interval (Eq. 4.2a).

questions.q: The SI unit of average velocity is…
questions.e: Velocity = metres ÷ seconds, so its SI unit is m s⁻¹ (m/s).

questions.q: Which of these quantities needs a direction to be described completely?
questions.e: Velocity has magnitude and direction; speed, distance and time have only numerical values.

questions.q: An object moving in a straight line covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. Its motion is…
questions.e: Equal distances in equal time intervals means constant speed – uniform motion.

questions.q: Sarang swims from one end of a 25 m pool to the other end and back in 50 s. His average speed and average velocity are…
questions.e: Distance = 50 m, so speed = 50/50 = 1 m s⁻¹. He returns to the start, so displacement and average velocity are 0.

questions.q: When can the average velocity of an object be zero while its average speed is not zero?
questions.a: When the object returns to its starting point
w: When it moves in one direction only
When its speed is constant in a straight line
questions.e: Returning to the start gives zero displacement (zero average velocity) though distance is not zero.

questions.q: The magnitude of average velocity equals the average speed when the object…
questions.a: moves along a straight line in one direction
w: comes back to its starting point
questions.e: Only then are distance travelled and magnitude of displacement equal.

questions.q: The reading of a vehicle's speedometer is nearly equal to…
questions.a: the magnitude of its velocity at that instant
w: its average velocity for the whole trip
questions.e: A speedometer shows the speed at an instant; the direction of the tyres gives the direction of velocity.

questions.q: Convert {k} km h⁻¹ into m s⁻¹.
During a road trip you drive {d} km north in {t1} h and then {d} km south in {t2} h. What is your average speed for the whole trip?
questions.e: Total distance = 2 × {d} = {dd} km; time = {t1} + {t2} = {tt} h. Average speed = {dd}/{tt} = {ans} km h⁻¹. (Average velocity is 0 – you are back at the start.)

questions.q: Two postmen start {D} yojanas apart and walk towards each other. One walks {a} yojanas per day and the other {b} yojanas per day. After how many days will they meet?
questions.e: Together they cover {a} + {b} = {s} yojanas per day, so time = {D} ÷ {s} = {ans} days. (Ganitakaumudi, 14th century CE.)

questions.q: A cyclist covers {s} m in {t} s. What is the average speed?
questions.e: Average speed = distance ÷ time = {s} m ÷ {t} s = {ans} m s⁻¹.

questions.q: Average acceleration is equal to…
questions.e: a = (v − u) / (t₂ − t₁) (Eq. 4.3c).

questions.q: The SI unit of acceleration is…
questions.e: Change in velocity (m s⁻¹) ÷ time (s) = m s⁻².

questions.q: A bus moves on a straight highway at a constant velocity of 20 m s⁻¹. Its acceleration is…
questions.e: Acceleration depends on how quickly velocity changes, not on how fast the object moves. Constant velocity → zero acceleration.

questions.q: A car moving forward on a straight road slows down. The direction of its acceleration is…
questions.a: opposite to the direction of its velocity
w: the same as the direction of its velocity
zero, because it is still moving forward
at right angles to its velocity
questions.e: When the magnitude of velocity decreases, acceleration acts opposite to velocity (it is negative).

questions.q: An object dropped from a height gains 9.8 m s⁻¹ of velocity every second. Its acceleration is…
questions.e: Equal change in velocity in equal intervals = constant acceleration; this is g, acting downwards.

questions.q: A girl's scooter speedometer shows a constant reading. Can the scooter be accelerating?
questions.a: Yes, if its direction of motion is changing, for example on a turn
w: No, constant speed always means zero acceleration
Only if it is going uphill
Only when the speedometer reads zero
questions.e: Velocity changes if its magnitude OR direction changes, so a turning scooter accelerates even at constant speed.

questions.q: The acceleration of an object can be caused by a change in…
questions.a: the magnitude of velocity, its direction, or both
w: only the position of the object
only the mass of the object
questions.e: Acceleration comes from any change in velocity – magnitude, direction or both.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and reaches a velocity of {v} m s⁻¹ in {t} s. What is its average acceleration?
A bus moving at {u} km h⁻¹ speeds up to {v} km h⁻¹ in {t} s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.e: u = {u} km h⁻¹ = {um} m s⁻¹, v = {v} km h⁻¹ = {vm} m s⁻¹. a = ({vm} − {um}) / {t} = {ans} m s⁻².

questions.q: A bus moving at {u} km h⁻¹ applies brakes and stops in {t} s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.e: u = {u} km h⁻¹ = {um} m s⁻¹, v = 0. a = (0 − {um}) / {t} = {ans} m s⁻². The minus sign means acceleration is opposite to velocity.

questions.q: A straight sloping line on a position–time graph shows that the object is moving with…
questions.e: Equal displacements in equal time intervals give a straight line: constant velocity.

questions.q: What does the slope of a position–time graph give?
questions.e: Slope = change in position ÷ change in time = velocity.

questions.q: What does this position–time graph tell you about the vehicle?
questions.a: It is at rest, 40 m from the origin
w: It is moving at 40 m s⁻¹
It is moving with constant acceleration
It is at rest at the origin
questions.e: A line parallel to the time axis means the position does not change: the object is stationary at 40 m.

questions.q: The position–time graph of a car is a curve that gets steeper with time. This shows…
questions.a: its velocity is increasing – it is accelerating
w: it is moving with constant velocity
questions.e: Increasing displacement in equal time intervals means increasing velocity (accelerated motion).

questions.q: Look at the position–time graphs of objects A and B. Which one has the greater velocity?
questions.a: B, because its line is steeper
w: A, because its line is lower
Both, because they start from the origin
It cannot be found without a table
questions.e: In the same time interval B's displacement is larger, so the slope (velocity) of B is greater.

questions.q: A position–time graph shows…
questions.a: how the position of an object changes with time
w: the actual route followed by the object
questions.e: A graph is not a route map: it shows position with respect to the origin at each instant.

questions.q: Objects A and B move along a straight line (see graph). Which statement is correct for the 10 s interval?
questions.a: Their average velocities are equal, but B has the greater average speed
w: A has the greater average velocity
questions.e: Same start and end positions → same displacement → equal average velocity. B goes to 50 m and comes back to 40 m, so it travels 60 m (more distance).

questions.q: Using the position–time graph, find the velocity of the vehicle.
questions.e: Slope = change in position ÷ change in time = {s} m ÷ {t} s = {ans} m s⁻¹.

questions.q: What does the slope of a velocity–time graph give?
questions.e: Slope = change in velocity ÷ change in time = acceleration.

questions.q: The area enclosed between a velocity–time graph and the time axis gives…
questions.e: Area = velocity × time = displacement.

questions.q: A velocity–time graph that is a straight line parallel to the time axis shows…
questions.e: No change in height → zero slope → acceleration is zero; velocity stays constant.

questions.q: What does this velocity–time graph show?
questions.a: Velocity decreasing with constant acceleration opposite to the velocity
questions.e: A straight line sloping down: velocity decreases by equal amounts in equal times (negative, constant acceleration).

questions.q: The velocity–time graph of a car is shown. What is its displacement in the time shown?
questions.e: Displacement = area of the rectangle = {v} m s⁻¹ × {t} s = {ans} m.

questions.q: A car starts from rest. Using the velocity–time graph, find its acceleration.
questions.e: Slope = change in velocity ÷ time = ({v} − 0) ÷ {t} = {ans} m s⁻².

questions.q: A car starts from rest. Using the velocity–time graph, find its displacement in the time shown.
questions.e: Displacement = area of the triangle = ½ × {t} s × {v} m s⁻¹ = {ans} m.

questions.q: Using the velocity–time graph, find the displacement of the object between 0 s and {t} s.
questions.e: Area = rectangle + triangle = ({u} × {t}) + ½ × {t} × ({v} − {u}) = {ans} m.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and speeds up uniformly to {v} m s⁻¹ in {t1} s, moves at this velocity for {t2} s, then brakes uniformly and stops in {t3} s. Find the total distance travelled.
questions.e: Area under the v–t graph = ½×{t1}×{v} + {t2}×{v} + ½×{t3}×{v} = {ans} m.

questions.q: Which kinematic equation gives the final velocity v?
questions.e: From a = (v − u)/t we get v = u + at (Eq. 4.4a).

questions.q: The kinematic equations can be used only when…
questions.e: They were derived for motion in a straight line with constant acceleration.

questions.q: Which equation relates v, u, a and s without using time t?
questions.e: Eliminating t from Eq. 4.4a and 4.4b gives v² = u² + 2as.

questions.q: The equation s = ½(u + v)t can be derived using the area of a…
questions.e: The area under a straight v–t line from u to v is a trapezium: ½(u + v) × t.

questions.q: The stopping distance of a vehicle after brakes are applied depends on…
questions.a: its speed, the road surface, the braking capacity and the driver's reaction time
w: only the colour of the vehicle
only the size of the engine
questions.e: That is why a safe distance from the vehicle ahead must be increased at higher speeds.

questions.q: With the same braking acceleration, if a car's speed doubles, its braking distance becomes…
questions.e: From v² = u² + 2as with v = 0, s = u²/2|a|. Doubling u makes s four times (e.g. 28.1 m → 112.5 m).

questions.q: A body starts with a velocity of {u} m s⁻¹ and accelerates at {a} m s⁻² for {t} s. What is its final velocity?
questions.e: v = u + at = {u} + {a} × {t} = {ans} m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A car starts from rest with a constant acceleration of {a} m s⁻². How far does it travel in {t} s?
questions.e: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × {a} × {t}² = {ans} m.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and its velocity reaches {v} m s⁻¹ in {t} s. What distance does it cover in this time?
questions.e: a = {v}/{t} = {a} m s⁻². s = ½at² = ½ × {a} × {t}² = {ans} m.

questions.q: A car moving at {u} km h⁻¹ brakes with an acceleration of –{a} m s⁻². How far does it travel before stopping?
questions.e: u = {u} km h⁻¹ = {um} m s⁻¹, v = 0. From v² = u² + 2as: s = u²/2a = {um}² ÷ (2 × {a}) = {ans} m.

questions.q: A motorbike moving at {u} m s⁻¹ with constant acceleration stops after travelling {s} m. What is its acceleration?
questions.e: 0 = u² + 2as → a = −u²/2s = −{u}² ÷ (2 × {s}) = {ans} m s⁻².

questions.q: A truck slows down uniformly from {u} km h⁻¹ to {v} km h⁻¹ in {t} s. How far does it travel in this time?
questions.e: u = {um} m s⁻¹, v = {vm} m s⁻¹. s = ½(u + v)t = ½ × ({um} + {vm}) × {t} = {ans} m.

questions.q: A bus at {u} km h⁻¹: the driver takes {tr} s to react, then brakes at –{a} m s⁻². What is the total distance covered before it stops?
questions.e: Reaction distance = {um} × {tr} = {rd} m. Braking distance = {um}² ÷ (2 × {a}) = {bd} m. Total = {ans} m.

questions.q: When an object moves in a circular path with constant speed, its motion is called…
questions.e: Circular path + constant (uniform) speed = uniform circular motion.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, what changes continuously?
questions.e: Speed is constant; only the direction of velocity keeps changing.

questions.q: Is uniform circular motion an accelerated motion?
questions.a: Yes, because the direction of velocity changes continuously
w: No, because the speed is constant
Only when the object speeds up
questions.e: Any change in velocity – even only in direction – means acceleration.

questions.q: After one complete revolution on a circle of radius R, the displacement of a child on a merry-go-round is…
questions.e: The child comes back to the starting position.

questions.q: The distance travelled in one complete revolution on a circle of radius R is…
questions.e: One revolution = circumference = 2πR.

questions.q: A marble moves around the inside of a ring on a table. When the ring is lifted, the marble…
questions.a: moves in a straight line in the direction it was moving at that instant
w: moves towards the centre of the ring
questions.e: Without the ring, it keeps moving in the direction of its velocity at that instant – along the tangent.

questions.q: In circular motion, the velocity of the object at any point is along…
questions.a: the tangent to the circle at that point
w: the radius, away from the centre
questions.e: The tangent touches the circle at only that point, in the direction of motion.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of motion in a plane (two dimensions)?
questions.a: The path of a kicked football
w: A train on a straight track
A swimmer in a straight lane
questions.e: A kicked ball moves forward and up/down at the same time – motion in two dimensions.

questions.q: A child goes half a revolution on a merry-go-round of radius R. The displacement is…
questions.e: After half a circle the child is at the opposite end of a diameter: 2R.

questions.q: Rohan studies from 6 PM to 7:30 PM. The minute hand of the clock is 7 cm long. What is the displacement of its tip?
questions.e: In 90 min the tip goes 1½ rounds: from 12 to 6, i.e., across a diameter = 2 × 7 = 14 cm. (Distance = 1.5 × 2π × 7 = 66 cm.)

questions.q: A child on a merry-go-round of radius {R} m completes one revolution in {T} s. What is the average speed? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: v = 2πR/T = 2 × 22/7 × {R} ÷ {T} = {ans} m s⁻¹. Average velocity for one full revolution is 0.

questions.q: The tip of a 7 cm long minute hand moves for {m} minutes. What distance does it travel? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: In {m} min the hand turns {m}/60 of a circle: distance = ({m}/60) × 2 × 22/7 × 7 = {ans} cm.

questions.q: A car moves along a straight road from x = +{p} m to x = −{n} m. What is its displacement?
questions.e: Displacement = final − initial = (−{n}) − (+{p}) = {ans} m (towards negative x).

questions.q: If you change the reference point (origin) for a moving car, what stays the same?
questions.a: Its displacement over a time interval
questions.e: Positions shift with the origin, but the change in position does not.

questions.q: A runner completes one and a half rounds of a circular track of radius {r} m. What is the magnitude of her displacement?
questions.e: After 1½ rounds she is diametrically opposite the start: displacement = 2r = {ans} m (distance = 3πr).

questions.q: A boy walks {a} m east, {b} m west and then {c} m east along a straight road. What is his displacement?
questions.e: Take east as +: {a} − {b} + {c} = {ans} m (distance = {a} + {b} + {c} m).

questions.q: A car covers the first half of a trip at {v1} km h⁻¹ and the second half (same distance) at {v2} km h⁻¹. What is its average speed?
questions.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 2 × {v1} × {v2} ÷ ({v1} + {v2}) = {ans} km h⁻¹ (not the simple average!).

questions.q: A train {L} m long moves at {v} km h⁻¹. How long does it take to pass a pole?
questions.e: {v} km h⁻¹ = {ms} m s⁻¹; time = {L} ÷ {ms} = {ans} s.

questions.q: A bus travels {d} km out and {d} km back in a total of {t} h, ending at the start. What is its average velocity for the whole trip?
questions.e: Displacement is 0, so average velocity is 0 km h⁻¹ – even though average speed is 2 × {d} ÷ {t} km h⁻¹.

questions.q: A car’s speed rises from {u} km h⁻¹ to {v} km h⁻¹ in {t} s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.e: Convert: ({v} − {u}) km h⁻¹ = {dv} m s⁻¹; a = {dv} ÷ {t} = {ans} m s⁻².

questions.q: A scooter moving at {u} m s⁻¹ brakes and stops in {t} s. What is its acceleration?
questions.e: a = (0 − {u}) ÷ {t} = {ans} m s⁻² – negative because it slows down.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A body moving with uniform speed in a circle is accelerating.
Reason (R): Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, and velocity changes when direction changes.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.e: Speed is constant but direction keeps changing, so velocity changes.

questions.q: Two cyclists start together. From the position–time graph, how far apart are they at t = {t} s?
questions.e: Positions: {b} × {t} and {a} × {t}. Gap = ({b} − {a}) × {t} = {ans} m.

questions.q: On a position–time graph, the lines of two cars cross each other. What does the crossing point tell you?
questions.a: Both cars are at the same position at that time
w: Both cars have the same velocity
The cars collide at the start
questions.e: Same x and same t → same place at the same moment.

questions.q: A position–time graph curves upward, getting steeper with time. The object is…
questions.e: Slope = velocity; an increasing slope means increasing velocity.

questions.q: From the velocity–time graph, find the displacement of the car in the time shown.
questions.e: Area of the trapezium = ½ × ({u} + {v}) × {t} = {ans} m.

questions.q: Part of a velocity–time graph lies below the time axis. What does this mean?
questions.a: The object is moving in the negative direction
questions.e: Negative velocity means motion opposite to the chosen positive direction.

questions.q: A car moving at {u} m s⁻¹ brakes with a deceleration of {a} m s⁻². How far does it travel before stopping?
questions.e: v² = u² + 2as with v = 0: s = {u}² ÷ (2 × {a}) = {ans} m.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up at {u} m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², how high does it rise?
questions.e: At the top v = 0: h = u² ÷ 2g = {u}² ÷ 20 = {ans} m.

questions.q: Car A starts from rest with acceleration {a} m s⁻² just as car B passes it at a steady {v} m s⁻¹. After how long does A catch B?
questions.e: Same distance: ½ × {a} × t² = {v} × t → t = 2 × {v} ÷ {a} = {ans} s.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration {a} m s⁻². What is its velocity after covering {s} m?
questions.e: v² = 2as = 2 × {a} × {s}; v = {ans} m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A stone tied to a string moves in a circle of radius {r} m, completing one revolution in {T} s. What is its speed? (Take π = 22/7.)
A car goes round a circular track of radius r once. What are its distance and displacement?
questions.e: It ends where it started.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, which quantity stays constant?
questions.e: Only the magnitude of velocity (speed) is constant.
